01_After_10th_Intermediate/BiPC/After_12.title: RMP / PMP 'Village Doctors' – Legal Facts Every Student Must Know

b.x: RMP here means 'Rural Medical Practitioner' and PMP means 'Private Medical Practitioner' – people who give treatment in villages without a recognised medical degree.
They are NOT Registered Medical Practitioners in law. 'RMP' does not mean 'registered'.
Under the National Medical Commission Act 2019 (Section 34), only a person registered with NMC/State Medical Council (MBBS or higher) may practise modern medicine.
Practising without registration: punishable with imprisonment up to 1 year and/or fine up to ₹5 lakh.
Prescribing antibiotics/steroids, giving injections, IV drips or running a 'clinic/hospital' without registration is illegal.
Telangana State Medical Council and the Drugs Control Administration conduct raids and file cases against unqualified practitioners.
Around 2015–2017, Telangana/AP proposed training RMPs/PMPs as 'Community Paramedics' (first-aid level, 6 months).
Doctors' associations challenged this in court. It does NOT give a licence to treat patients as a doctor.
Do NOT pay for any 'RMP certificate course' – it gives no legal right to practise.
Choose a recognised, legal health career instead (see next file).
